title: Digest downloads trust filenames as filesystem paths
reasoning: filename crosses the Ghostwriter/backend boundary and is reused directly as a child path. Path separators or an absolute path can escape the intended Epilogue download directory or overwrite another app-accessible file, depending on platform path handling and app storage permissions.
reproduction: Call downloadDigest with a filename such as ../other-file.epub or an absolute path and observe that File(documentsDir, filename) does not enforce containment in documentsDir.
recommendation: Reject absolute paths and path separators, normalize to a safe basename, and verify outputFile.canonicalPath remains inside documentsDir.canonicalPath before writing. Consider writing to a temp file and atomically renaming after validation.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only discovered download test targets SharedGhostwriterAdapter raw bytes, not GhostwriterRepository filesystem path validation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GhostwriterRepository download test that passes traversal and absolute filenames and asserts the repository rejects them before opening an output stream.
minimumFixScope: GhostwriterRepository downloadDigest and downloadDigestById output path construction.

history.reasoning: The original evidence path still exists, but the unsafe File(documentsDir, filename) writes in GhostwriterRepository.downloadDigest are no longer present at the cited locations. Both shared-client and Retrofit branches now call resolveDigestOutputFile(documentsDir, filename) before opening the output stream, and downloadDigestById also uses the same helper for outputFilename. The helper rejects blank names, '/', '\\', '.', '..', non-basename values, and verifies the canonical output path stays under the canonical Epilogue directory. A current regression test file exists for accepting safe basenames and rejecting traversal/absolute paths. I attempted the focused Gradle test, but the read-only sandbox prevented Gradle from opening its wrapper lock file, so runtime verification could not complete in this environment.
